sentences.cn_text: 这位来自埃文河畔斯特拉特福的文法学校学生取得了学术上的重大突破，开创性研究表明莎士比亚确实有益于儿童的读写能力和情感发展。
sentences.en_text: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children’s literacy and emotional development.

sentences.cn_text: 但前提是你要将其表演出来。
sentences.en_text: But only if you act him out.

sentences.cn_text: 一项研究发现，采用「排练室」方法教授莎士比亚能够拓宽儿童的词汇量，增强其写作的复杂性，并提升他们的情感素养。
sentences.en_text: A study found that a “rehearsal room” approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children’s vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy.

sentences.cn_text: 委托该研究的皇家莎士比亚剧团的杰奎·奥汉隆表示：「研究表明，演员的工作方式对儿童使用语言的方式以及他们对自我的认知产生重大影响。」
sentences.en_text: “The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves,” Jacqui O’Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.

sentences.cn_text: 这项随机对照试验涉及45所公立小学的数百名五年级学生——年龄为九至十岁——这些学校此前未曾「接触过皇家莎士比亚剧团的教学法」。学生被分为实验组和对照组,并被要求完成写作任务,例如以《暴风雨》中费迪南德的身份,在海难后写一封瓶中信。
sentences.en_text: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils — aged nine and ten — at 45 state primary schools that had not been “previously exposed to RSC pedagogy.” They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand following the shipwreck in The Tempest.

sentences.cn_text: 实验组学生被安排了一项30分钟的戏剧活动来配合该段落的学习。
sentences.en_text: The target group were given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.

sentences.cn_text: 经同行评审的结果显示,实验组学生使用了更广泛的词汇,运用了「被归类为更复杂或更罕见」的词语,且写作篇幅更长。
sentences.en_text: The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words “classed as more sophisticated or rarer”, and wrote at greater length.

sentences.cn_text: 他们还「似乎更能适应角色写作……而对照组学生想象的是自己在海难中的反应,实验组学生则设身处地体会文学角色,并表达该角色的情感」。
sentences.en_text: They also “appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character’s emotion”.

sentences.cn_text: 皇家莎士比亚剧团本周发布的《行动的时机》研究还发现,对照组学生依赖于诸如椰子树等「荒岛陈词滥调」,而实验组学生则「更具扩展性,呈现了更广阔的天空、海洋和大气状况的画面」。
sentences.en_text: The Time to Act study, which is published by the RSC this week, also found that while control pupils relied on “desert island clichés” such as palm trees, target pupils were “more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions”.

sentences.cn_text: 奥汉隆表示,她最为惊讶的是实验组儿童写作中体现出的「情感素养」,以及他们「在写作中更具韧性,更加乐观」。
sentences.en_text: O’Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the “emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children’s writing” and that they were “more resilient in their writing, more hopeful”.

sentences.cn_text: 她补充道:「情感理解非常明显,这可能与排练室过程有关,在那里你习惯于尝试通过想象来体会。」
sentences.en_text: She added “The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through.

sentences.cn_text: 他们能够自如地描述不同的情感状态,而戏剧活动的一部分就是让自己设身处地体会不同的角色。她表示,该研究显示了将艺术融入教育的重要性。
sentences.en_text: They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes.” The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.

sentences.cn_text: 但这一结果能否在任何其他剧作家身上得以复制?
sentences.en_text: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist?

sentences.cn_text: 奥汉隆表示还需要更多研究,但她指出,莎士比亚使用了约2万个词汇,而日常语言仅约2000个词汇,这为儿童的生活带来了「语言的大幅扩展」,并且结合了儿童「用整个身体使语言变得生动」的方式。
sentences.en_text: O’Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare’s use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a “massive expansion of language into children’s lives”, which was combined with children “using their whole bodies to bring words to life”.
